text:
Mia Rivera: @channel seeing a sudden customer spike of 503/500 for hosted inference starting ~09:10 UTC. Multiple customers complaining about timeouts and errors. Notably: repeated 503s from the API gateway, and some backend logs show abrupt worker exits. Any idea?

Alex Chen: Which pool/region? Any correlating deploys?

Mia Rivera: us-west-2, hosted-prod-gpu-pool-4. No deploys from product since 08:45. Support ticket from customer 'BlueArc' with repro steps attached.

Sanjay Patel: I'm looking at infra metrics — GPU memory use jumped around 09:08 for that pool, then a bunch of pods restarted. Crashloop logs show 'segfault' and 'aborted'.

Emily Park: Repro from support: POST /v1/generate with long context (~18k tokens) using model redwood-7b-quantized. They got repeated 503s.

Mia Rivera: tagging @oncall-bot so we have pager coverage.

oncall-bot: Pager duty incident created: PD-4821. Escalation to Eng-runtime and Eng-sre.

Alex Chen: Can someone paste the kube logs?

Sanjay Patel: Pasting snippets: ```
==> kubectl logs infer-runner-54f2 -n hosted
[2025-06-14T09:09:12Z] INFO Starting inference runner (commit abc123)
[2025-06-14T09:09:45Z] WARN Long request detected: 110s
[2025-06-14T09:09:47Z] ERROR Received signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
[2025-06-14T09:09:47Z] ERROR Backtrace:
#0 0x7f3a1c0f in llm::attention::compute
#1 0x7f3a2b2d in llm::kernels::forward
#2 0x55c77a3b main
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Emily Park: System dmesg shows OOM killer fired: ```
[  123.456789] Out of memory: Killed process 31245 (infer-runner) total-vm:20480000kB, anon-rss:8192000kB, file-rss:0kB
[  123.456790] Kill process 31245 (infer-runner) score 953 or sacrifice child
```

Mia Rivera: So it looks like GPU memory blowup + segfault in attention kernel. Any known regressions in quantized kernels?

Alex Chen: We merged a micro-optim change to KV cache prefetch in last release (deploy 08:30) but product said stable. Could interact with certain long-context inputs.

Sanjay Patel: I pulled the core and ran gdb on a similar build. Backtrace points to fused-attn kernel: ```
#0 0x7f3b0e6a in fused_attn::run
#1 0x7f3b0f8c in fused_attn::dispatch
#2 0x55d4bcc1 in inference::step
```

Emily Park: Customer reports they started seeing it after switching to the quantized model variant yesterday. Rolling them back to the FP16 endpoint temporarily stops the errors.

Mia Rivera: OK mitigation plan ideas?

Alex Chen: Short term: 1) Increase pool autoscale buffer for hosted-prod-gpu-pool-4 by +50% to avoid memory pressure, 2) add an automatic fallback rule in the gateway to route to FP16 variant on 500/503 spikes, 3) temporarily pin affected customers to FP16.

Sanjay Patel: Agreed. I'm also going to taint nodes that show repeat OOMs and drain to prevent more restarts. Working on a script.

Emily Park: Support will notify affected customers of a temporary rollback to FP16 and request sample payload causing the blowup (we need exact prompt).

Mia Rivera: Who owns a root-cause PR? We need a safe rollback of the micro-optim change if it's implicated.

Alex Chen: I'll bisect the change set. If fused-attn changes are culprit, we'll revert and cut a hotfix build. ETA 2-3 hours for initial bisect.

Sanjay Patel: I've run a repro locally with the quantized model + long context and reproduced an out-of-memory followed by cuda segmentation fault: ```
CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

Mia Rivera: Any quick config toggles? Perhaps limit max_input_length for quantized endpoints to 12k tokens until fix?

Emily Park: We can push a temporary policy: reject >12k token requests with 413 or route to FP16. I'll prepare the gate rule.

oncall-bot: Runbook suggestion: if GPU OOMs + segfaults observed, immediately (1) set autoscale target to 2x, (2) apply gateway fallback to stable FP16 variant, (3) gather core dumps and dmesg, (4) open a regression PR.

Mia Rivera: Good. Sanjay, can you collect core dump and upload to S3? Use s3://redwood-debug/infer-core/1749999999/ and mark with customer id and pod name.

Sanjay Patel: Uploading now. Also captured: ```
infer-runner-54f2 core file: /var/crash/core.infer-runner.31245
gdb --batch -ex 'bt' -ex 'info threads' /path/to/binary core.infer-runner.31245 > /tmp/core_bt.txt
```

Alex Chen: Bisection update: the KV-prefetch refactor (PR #971) introduced a subtle out-of-bounds under specific block lengths. I have a minimal repro. Preparing revert PR.

Emily Park: Support note drafted: "We observed GPU OOMs and crashes for quantized variant with very long contexts. As a precaution we've reverted affected customers to a non-quantized variant and applied temporary guards. We're working on a hotfix." Will send after PR merged.

Mia Rivera: Postmortem checklist: timeline, affected customers, mitigation, root cause (PR #971 OOB), fix (revert + unit test), rollout plan, monitoring: add a detector for sudden GPU memory spike on single pod.

Sanjay Patel: Adding core analysis and memory profiler traces to the incident bundle.

Alex Chen: Revert PR created: https://github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/1024 (hotfix revert of PR #971). Running CI now.

Mia Rivera: Once CI green, let's coordinate a hotfix rollout to hosted-prod-gpu-pool-4 at low-traffic window + follow-up gradual ramp.

support-bot: Customer notifications dispatched to 3 affected accounts. Ticket IDs: SUP-8810, SUP-8812, SUP-8813.

Mia Rivera: Thanks team. Keep updates here as actions complete.

Alex Chen: CI passed for revert. Planning hotfix rollout in 20 minutes with canary on 2 pods then full roll.

Sanjay Patel: Canary showing stable memory behavior after revert. No segfaults in 30m. Scaling gradual now.

Emily Park: Customers acknowledged and closed with 'thanks'.

Mia Rivera: Incident resolved — marking timeline and starting postmortem doc. Great cross-team work. :party_parrot:

oncall-bot: Incident PD-4821 marked RESOLVED at 2025-06-14T12:06:39Z.

Mia Rivera: Postmortem owner assigned: Alex Chen. Expected ship: postmortem + monitoring changes by EOD tomorrow.
